drills.solution: $\delta = \ln\dfrac{{u1}}{{u2}} \approx$ **{dl:num4}**. Then $\zeta = \dfrac{\delta}{\sqrt{4\pi^2 + \delta^2}} \approx {z:num4}$ and $Q = \dfrac{1}{2\zeta} \approx$ **{Q:num2}** (the shortcut $\pi/\delta$ gives nearly the same for light damping).

drills.title: Resonant frequency and Q of an RLC circuit
drills.prompt: A series RLC circuit has $L = {L}$ H, $C = {cap}$ F and $R = {R}$ Ω. Find its natural frequency $\omega_0$ and its quality factor $Q$, each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution: With $m \to L$, $\gamma \to R$, $k \to 1/C$: $\omega_0 = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{LC}} \approx$ **{w0:sig3} rad/s**, and $Q = \dfrac1R\sqrt{\dfrac LC} \approx$ **{Q:sig3}**. (The bandwidth is $R/L = {dw:sig3}$ rad/s, and $\omega_0/(R/L)$ gives the same $Q$.)

drills.title: Sag of a simply supported beam
drills.prompt: A beam {L} m long is simply supported at both ends and carries a uniform load of {w} N/m. Its flexural rigidity is $EI = {EI}$ N·m². Find its largest deflection in millimeters, to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution: The largest sag is at the middle: $y_{\max} = \dfrac{5wL^4}{384EI} = \dfrac{5({w:sig6})({L4:sig6})}{384({EI})}$ m $\approx$ **{d:sig3} mm**.

drills.title: Euler buckling load
drills.prompt: A slender column {L} m long has $EI = {EI}$ N·m². Find its critical buckling load in kN (3 significant figures) if both ends are pinned, and if instead the base is clamped and the top is free.
drills.solution: Pinned ends: $P_{\text{cr}} = \dfrac{\pi^2EI}{L^2} = \dfrac{\pi^2({EI})}{{L2:sig6}}$ N $\approx$ **{P:sig3} kN**. Clamped–free: a quarter of that, $\dfrac{\pi^2EI}{4L^2} \approx$ **{P4:sig3} kN**.

drills.title: Transform of a periodic pulse train
drills.prompt: A periodic input equals {k} for $0 \le t < {w}$ and 0 for ${w} \le t < {T}$, repeating with period {T}. Find its Laplace transform at $s = {s0}$, to 4 decimal places.
drills.solution: One period: $\displaystyle\int_0^{w} {k:coef}e^{-st}\,dt = \dfrac{{k:coef}(1 - e^{-{w:coef}s})}{s}$. Divide by $1 - e^{-{T:coef}s}$ (the full period is {T}): $F(s) = \dfrac{{k:coef}(1 - e^{-{w:coef}s})}{s(1 - e^{-{T:coef}s})}$. At $s = {s0}$ this is **{F:num4}**.

drills.title: Periodic steady state under a square wave
drills.prompt: The equation $y' + {a:coef}y = {b:coef}f(t)$ is driven by the on/off square wave $f$ (1 for a time {p}, then 0 for a time {p}, repeating). Find the maximum $M$ and minimum $m$ of the periodic steady state, to 4 decimal places.
drills.solution: While the input is on, $y$ moves from $m$ toward the equilibrium $\dfrac{{b}}{{a}}$: $M = \dfrac{{b}}{{a}} - \left(\dfrac{{b}}{{a}} - m\right)r$ with $r = e^{-{ap}} \approx {r:num4}$. While it is off, $y$ decays: $m = Mr$. Substituting, $M(1 - r^2) = \dfrac{{b}}{{a}}(1 - r)$, so $M = \dfrac{{b}}{{a}}\cdot\dfrac{1}{1 + r} \approx$ **{M:num4}** and $m = Mr \approx$ **{m:num4}**.

drills.title: Transform of t times a damped sine
drills.prompt: Use $\mathcal{L}\{tf(t)\} = -F'(s)$ to find $\mathcal{L}\{t\,e^{{a:coef}t}\sin {bb:coef}t\}$.
drills.solution: Without the $t$: $F(s) = \mathcal{L}\{e^{{a:coef}t}\sin {bb:coef}t\} = \dfrac{{bb}}{(s {na:signed})^2 + {bsq}}$. By the chain rule, $F'(s) = -\dfrac{{bb}\cdot2(s {na:signed})}{\left((s {na:signed})^2 + {bsq}\right)^2}$. So the transform is $-F'(s) =$ **$\dfrac{{b2}(s {na:signed})}{\left((s {na:signed})^2 + {bsq}\right)^2}$**.

drills.title: An integral from a transform
drills.prompt: Use $\mathcal{L}\left\{\dfrac{\sin kt}{t}\right\} = \arctan\dfrac{k}{s}$ to evaluate $\displaystyle\int_0^\infty e^{-{a:coef}t}\,\frac{\sin {bb:coef}t}{t}\,dt$ to 4 decimal places.
drills.solution: The integral is the Laplace transform of $\dfrac{\sin {bb:coef}t}{t}$ evaluated at $s = {a}$, so it equals $\arctan\dfrac{{bb}}{{a}} \approx$ **{v:num4}** (radians).

drills.title: Final value of a step response
drills.prompt: A system with transfer function $H(s) = \dfrac{{p:coef}s + {q}}{s^2 + {bb:coef}s + {c}}$ starts at rest and receives the step input $g(t) = {k}u_0(t)$. Find $\displaystyle\lim_{t\to\infty}y(t)$ as an exact fraction.
drills.solution: $Y(s) = H(s)\cdot\dfrac{{k}}{s}$, so $sY = {k:coef}H(s)$. Its poles are the roots of $s^2 + {bb:coef}s + {c}$, which has positive coefficients, so both lie in the left half-plane and the final value theorem applies: $\lim y = \lim_{s\to0}{k:coef}H(s) = {k:coef}H(0) = \dfrac{{kq}}{{c}} =$ **{fv:frac}**.

drills.title: Stability limit of a cubic
drills.prompt: The polynomial $s^3 + {a:coef}s^2 + {bb:coef}s + K$ has all its roots in the open left half-plane exactly when $0 < K < K_{\max}$. Find $K_{\max}$, and the angular frequency $\omega$ of the steady oscillation (the roots on the imaginary axis) when $K = K_{\max}$, to 3 decimal places.
drills.solution: Routh–Hurwitz for a cubic $a_3s^3 + a_2s^2 + a_1s + a_0$: all coefficients positive and $a_2a_1 > a_3a_0$. Here that is $K > 0$ and ${a}\cdot{bb} > K$, so $K_{\max} =$ **{K}**. At $K = {K}$ the polynomial factors as $(s + {a})(s^2 + {bb})$, with roots $-{a}$ and $\pm i\sqrt{{bb}}$, so $\omega = \sqrt{{bb}} \approx$ **{w:dp3}**.

drills.title: Natural frequencies of two coupled masses
drills.prompt: Two masses of {m} kg each sit on a frictionless track. Springs $k_1 = {k1}$ N/m and $k_3 = {k3}$ N/m join them to the walls, and a coupling spring $k_2 = {k2}$ N/m joins them to each other. Find the two natural frequencies in rad/s, smaller first, to 2 decimal places.
drills.solution: The stiffness matrix is $K = \begin{bmatrix} {K11} & -{k2} \\ -{k2} & {K22} \end{bmatrix}$, and dividing by the mass gives $M^{-1}K = \begin{bmatrix} {a:num4} & -{c:num4} \\ -{c:num4} & {d:num4} \end{bmatrix}$. Its trace is ${T:num4}$ and its determinant ${Dt:num4}$, so the eigenvalues $\omega^2$ solve $\mu^2 - {T:num4}\mu + {Dt:num4} = 0$: $\mu = \dfrac{{T:num4} \pm {sq:num4}}{2}$, that is ${mu1:num4}$ and ${mu2:num4}$. These are the squared frequencies, so $\omega_1 = \sqrt{{mu1:num4}} \approx$ **{w1:num2}** and $\omega_2 = \sqrt{{mu2:num4}} \approx$ **{w2:num2}** rad/s.

drills.title: Energy transfer between weakly coupled oscillators
drills.prompt: Two {m} kg masses each have a wall spring of {k} N/m and are joined by a weak coupling spring of {kap} N/m. Mass 1 is released from rest with mass 2 at equilibrium. When does all the motion first pass to mass 2? Give the time in seconds to 1 decimal place.
drills.solution: The in-phase mode has $\omega_1 = \sqrt{{k}/{m}} \approx {w1:num4}$ and the out-of-phase mode $\omega_2 = \sqrt{({k} + 2 \cdot {kap})/{m}} = \sqrt{{k2}/{m}} \approx {w2:num4}$ rad/s. The envelope of mass 1 is $\cos\big(\tfrac{\omega_2 - \omega_1}{2}t\big)$, which first reaches zero at $t = \dfrac{\pi}{\omega_2 - \omega_1} = \dfrac{\pi}{{dw:num4}} \approx$ **{tt:num1} s**.

drills.title: Peak of the second tank in a chain
drills.prompt: Pure water flows at {F} L/min into tank 1 ({V1} L), from tank 1 into tank 2 ({V2} L), and out of tank 2. Tank 1 starts with {Q0} g of salt and tank 2 with none. When does the salt in tank 2 peak, and how much is there then? Give the time to 2 decimal places and the amount to 1 decimal place.
drills.solution: The rate constants are $a = {F}/{V1} = {a:num4}$ and $b = {F}/{V2} = {b:num4}$ per minute, so $Q_1' = -aQ_1$ and $Q_2' = aQ_1 - bQ_2$. Then $Q_1 = {Q0}e^{-at}$ and, with $Q_2(0) = 0$, $Q_2 = \dfrac{{Q0}a}{b - a}\big(e^{-at} - e^{-bt}\big)$. Setting $Q_2' = 0$ gives $ae^{-at} = be^{-bt}$, so $t = \dfrac{\ln(a/b)}{a - b} \approx$ **{tp:num2} min**, when $Q_2 \approx$ **{Qp:num1} g**.

drills.title: Characteristic polynomial of a 3×3 matrix
drills.prompt: For $A = \begin{bmatrix} {p11} & {p12} & {p13} \\ {p21} & {p22} & {p23} \\ {p31} & {p32} & {p33} \end{bmatrix}$, write $\det(\lambda I - A) = \lambda^3 + a_1\lambda^2 + a_2\lambda + a_3$ and find $a_1$, $a_2$ and $a_3$.
drills.solution: $a_1 = -\operatorname{tr}A = -({trA}) =$ **{a1}**. The principal minors (delete row and column 1, 2, 3 in turn) are ${mi1}$, ${mi2}$ and ${mi3}$, so $a_2 =$ **{a2}**. Expanding along the first row, $\det A = {dt}$, so $a_3 = -\det A =$ **{a3}**. Routh–Hurwitz: the origin is asymptotically stable exactly when $a_1 > 0$, $a_3 > 0$ and $a_1a_2 > a_3$; here $a_1a_2 = {prod}$.

drills.title: Critical feedback strength for a three-stage loop
drills.prompt: A feedback loop $x_1' = -{p:coef}x_1 - kx_3$, $x_2' = x_1 - {q:coef}x_2$, $x_3' = x_2 - {r:coef}x_3$ has $\det(\lambda I - A) = (\lambda + {p})(\lambda + {q})(\lambda + {r}) + k$. Find the critical feedback strength $k_c$ (the steady state is stable for $0 \le k < k_c$ and unstable for $k > k_c$), and the angular frequency of the oscillation that appears at that $k$ (2 decimal places).
drills.solution: Expanding, $\det(\lambda I - A) = \lambda^3 + {s1}\lambda^2 + {s2}\lambda + ({s3} + k)$. Routh–Hurwitz needs $a_1 = {s1} > 0$, $a_3 = {s3} + k > 0$ and $a_1a_2 > a_3$: ${s1} \cdot {s2} = {s12} > {s3} + k$, so $k < {s12} - {s3}$. The threshold is $k_c =$ **{kc}**. There the polynomial is $(\lambda + {s1})(\lambda^2 + {s2})$, with roots $\pm i\sqrt{{s2}}$, so $\omega = \sqrt{{s2}} \approx$ **{w:num2}**.

drills.title: Indicial roots at a regular singular point
drills.prompt: Find the roots of the indicial equation of $2x^2y'' {p:signedcoef}xy' + (x {q:signed})y = 0$ at the regular singular point $x = 0$. Exact fractions or integers.
drills.solution: Divide by $2x^2$: $xp(x) = \dfrac{{p}}{2}$ and $x^2q(x) = \dfrac{x {q:signed}}{2}$, so $p_0 = \dfrac{{p}}{2}$ and $q_0 = \dfrac{{q}}{2}$. The indicial equation $r(r - 1) + p_0r + q_0 = 0$, times 2, is $2r^2 {pm2:signedcoef}r {q:signed} = 0$. Its roots (by factoring or the quadratic formula) are $r_1 =$ **{r1:frac}** and $r_2 =$ **{r2:frac}**.

drills.title: Coefficients of a Frobenius series
drills.prompt: The equation ${m}xy'' + y' {k:signedcoef}y = 0$ has indicial roots $r = 0$ and a nonzero root $r$. For the Frobenius series $y = \sum_{n=0}^\infty a_nx^{n+r}$ with the nonzero root and $a_0 = {a0}$, find $r$, $a_1$ and $a_2$. Exact fractions.
drills.solution: Substituting, the power $x^{n+r-1}$ collects ${m}(n + r)(n + r - 1)a_n + (n + r)a_n {k:signedcoef}a_{n-1} = 0$. For $n = 0$: $r\big({m}(r - 1) + 1\big) = 0$, so $r = 0$ or $r = 1 - \dfrac{1}{{m}} =$ **{rr:frac}**. The recurrence is $a_n = \dfrac{{nk:coef}a_{n-1}}{(n + r)\big({m}(n + r - 1) + 1\big)}$. With $r = {rr:texfrac}$ the denominators are ${d1}$ for $n = 1$ and ${d2}$ for $n = 2$, so $a_1 = \dfrac{({nk})({a0})}{{d1}} =$ **{a1:frac}** and $a_2 = \dfrac{({nk})\left({a1:texfrac}\right)}{{d2}} =$ **{a2:frac}**.

drills.title: Steady temperature in a rectangular plate
drills.prompt: A plate $0 < x < {wid}$, $0 < y < {ht}$ has its left, right and bottom edges held at 0 and its top edge at $u(x, {ht}) = {A}\sin\dfrac{{n:coef}\pi x}{{wid}}$. Find the steady temperature at $({x0}, {y0})$ to 4 decimal places.
drills.solution: The top data is a single sine mode, so $u = {A}\,\dfrac{\sinh({k:num4}\,y)}{\sinh({k:num4} \cdot {ht})}\sin({k:num4}\,x)$, where ${k:num4} = \dfrac{{n:coef}\pi}{{wid}}$. At $({x0}, {y0})$ the sinh ratio is ${ratio:num4}$ and the sine is ${sn:num4}$, so $u \approx$ **{u:num4}**.

drills.title: Laplace's equation in a disk
drills.prompt: A disk of radius ${R}$ has edge temperature $f(\theta) = {c0} {c1:signedcoef}\cos\theta {c2:signedcoef}\sin 2\theta$. Find the steady temperature at $r = {r0}$, $\theta = {th}$ (4 decimal places) and at the center.
drills.solution: Each Fourier mode of the edge data is scaled by $(r/R)^n$: $u = {c0} {c1:signedcoef}\left(\dfrac{r}{{R}}\right)\cos\theta {c2:signedcoef}\left(\dfrac{r}{{R}}\right)^2\sin 2\theta$. At $r = {r0}$, $\theta = {th}$: the cosine term is ${t1:num4}$ and the sine term is ${t2:num4}$, so $u \approx$ **{u:num4}**. At the center only the average remains: **{c0}**.

drills.title: A plucked pulse on a long string
drills.prompt: A long string with wave speed $a = {a}$ starts at rest in the shape $f(x) = {H}\max\left(0,\ 1 - \dfrac{|x|}{{w}}\right)$ (a triangle of height {H} and half-width {w}). Find $u({x0}, {t0})$. (Exact decimal or fraction.)
drills.solution: With $g = 0$, d'Alembert's formula is $u = \tfrac12\big[f(x - at) + f(x + at)\big]$. Here $x - at = {lo}$ and $x + at = {hi}$, where $f({lo}) = {fl:num4}$ and $f({hi}) = {fh:num4}$. So $u = \tfrac12({fl:num4} + {fh:num4}) =$ **{u:num4}**.

drills.title: A string struck with an initial velocity
drills.prompt: A long string with wave speed $a = {a}$ is flat at $t = 0$, and is struck so that its initial velocity is $g(x) = {V}$ for $|x| < {w}$ and 0 elsewhere. Find $u({x0}, {t0})$. (Exact decimal or fraction.)
drills.solution: With $f = 0$, $u = \dfrac{1}{2a}\displaystyle\int_{x-at}^{x+at}g(s)\,ds$, and $g = {V}$ only on $(-{w}, {w})$. The interval of integration is $[{lo}, {hi}]$; its overlap with $[-{w}, {w}]$ is $[{lft}, {rgt}]$, of length ${len}$. So $u = \dfrac{{V} \cdot {len}}{2 \cdot {a}} =$ **{u:num4}**.

drills.title: Derivative of V along trajectories
drills.prompt: For the system $x' = {a:coef}x {b:signedcoef}y$, $y' = {c:coef}x {d:signedcoef}y {k:signedcoef}x^3$ and $V = {p:coef}x^2 + {q:coef}y^2$, find $\dot V$ (the derivative of $V$ along trajectories) at the point $({x0}, {y0})$.
drills.solution: $\dot V = V_x\,x' + V_y\,y' = {P2}x \cdot x' + {Q2}y \cdot y'$. At $({x0}, {y0})$ the right-hand sides are $x' = {F0}$ and $y' = {G0}$, so $\dot V = {P2} \cdot ({x0}) \cdot ({F0}) + {Q2} \cdot ({y0}) \cdot ({G0}) =$ **{vd}**.

drills.title: When is a quadratic form positive definite?
drills.prompt: The quadratic form $V = {a:coef}x^2 + kxy + {c:coef}y^2$ is positive definite exactly when $|k| < K$. Find $K$ (exact, or to 2 decimal places).
drills.solution: $ax^2 + bxy + cy^2$ is positive definite exactly when the $x^2$ coefficient is positive and $4ac - b^2 > 0$. Here the $x^2$ coefficient is ${a} > 0$, and the second condition reads $4 \cdot {a} \cdot {c} - k^2 > 0$, that is $k^2 < {F}$. So $|k| < \sqrt{{F}}$, and $K = \sqrt{{F}} \approx$ **{K:num2}**.

drills.title: A disk inside the basin of attraction
drills.prompt: For $x' = -{a:coef}x {m:signedcoef}xy^2$, $y' = -{a:coef}y {m:signedcoef}x^2y$, use $V = x^2 + y^2$. Find the radius $R$ of the largest open disk around the origin on which $\dot V < 0$ at every point except the origin (2 decimal places).
drills.solution: $\dot V = 2x(-{a:coef}x {m:signedcoef}xy^2) + 2y(-{a:coef}y {m:signedcoef}x^2y) = -{A2}(x^2 + y^2) + {M4}x^2y^2$. On the circle of radius $r$, $x^2y^2 = \tfrac14r^4\sin^2 2\theta$ is at most $\tfrac14r^4$, with equality on the diagonals. So the largest value of $\dot V$ on that circle is $-{A2}r^2 + {m:coef}r^4 = -r^2\big({A2} - {m:coef}r^2\big)$, which is negative exactly when $r^2 < \dfrac{{A2}}{{m}} = {Rs:num4}$. So $R = \sqrt{{Rs:num4}} \approx$ **{R:num2}**. The disk can't be any bigger: the saddles $(\pm{E:num4}, \pm{E:num4})$ lie on its edge.
